indicating that solid-solution strengthening mechanisms proposed for conventional alloys operate also for HEAs and MEAs
the temperature dependence of σY of these alloys seems to be well interpreted in terms of thermally activated dislocation glide

conflicts.topic: effect of short-range ordering on yield strength of CrCoNi
claims: furnace cooling from 1273 K after homogenization at 1473 K for 48 h gives a 25% increase in yield strength
low-temperature annealing at 873 or 973 K for 384 h followed by water quenching after homogenization at 1373 K for 24 h shows no significant effect of SRO on sigma_Y

evidence.quote: On the other hand, no significant effect of SRO on σY is observed for tensile-tested CrCoNi polycrystals subjected to low-temperature annealing (at either 873 or 973 K for 384 h followed by water quenching) to induce SRO after homogenization at 1373 K for 24 h.
